lessons.title: Traditional industries: jute, tea, silk and crafts
lessons.summary: The state's signature industries (jute, tea, silk and handloom), the numbers examiners ask, and the GI-tagged products of West Bengal.

sections.html:
Take a boat down the Hooghly past Titagarh or Budge Budge and you see the tall chimneys of jute mills on both banks. Jute is Bengal's oldest organised industry and still its most distinctive.

WhatDetail
Composite jute mills in India (as of December 2025)120
Of these, in West Bengal89, the most of any state
Wheremostly along the Hooghly (Titagarh, Bhadreswar, Budge Budge, Rishra and others)
WB share of India's raw juteroughly three-quarters
Main jute districtsNadia, Murshidabad, North 24 Parganas, Malda
India's share of world jute goodsabout 75%
Jobsabout 3.7 lakh workers in organised mills and diversified units
Farm families supportedabout 40 lakh

A "composite" mill does every step under one roof, from raw fibre to finished sacks and cloth. There are two varieties: white jute (Corchorus capsularis) and tossa jute (Corchorus olitorius).

Number trick

Tossa = olitorius: both have an O. White jute = capsularis. Mills: 89 of 120, about three-quarters, and West Bengal also grows about three-quarters of India's raw jute. Say "three-quarters twice".

Examiner's twist

India is #1 in jute goods but second in raw jute area to Bangladesh, depending on the year and measure. Read the question carefully: goods or fibre?

Remember for the exam

89 of 120 mills in WB (Dec 2025). India makes about 75% of world jute goods. Tossa = olitorius, white = capsularis.

Tossa jute is botanically:

  1. Hibiscus cannabinus
  2. Corchorus capsularis
  3. Corchorus olitorius
The two jute species

Corchorus capsularisCorchorus olitorius

sections.h: The law that keeps the mills running
sections.html:
Every government sack

Every sack of wheat or rice that government agencies buy must be a jute sack. That rule, the Jute Packaging Materials Act of 1987, is a big reason most of India's jute mills still run along the Hooghly while synthetic bags took over everywhere else.

The government's foodgrain buying works like a guaranteed big customer for the mills.

Institution or lawWhat it does
Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory Use in Packing Commodities) Act, 1987 (JPM Act)requires foodgrains and sugar to be packed in jute bags
National Jute BoardHQ Kolkata
Jute Corporation of India (JCI)buys raw jute at MSP (minimum support price: the floor price the government guarantees farmers)
Remember for the exam

Jute bags for foodgrains and sugar: JPM Act, 1987. National Jute Board and JCI are headquartered in Kolkata.

Which Act makes jute bags compulsory for packing foodgrains?

  1. Jute Packaging Materials Act, 1987
  2. Jute Control Act, 1948
  3. Essential Commodities Act, 1955

A cup of Darjeeling tea is light and fragrant; the strong, dark tea at a roadside stall is usually CTC. Bengal makes both. First keep two labels apart: how a tea is made (the method) and what type it is.

The two labels:

LabelWhat it means
Method: orthodoxthe leaf is rolled and twisted, with longer oxidation; gives whole-leaf and broken grades
Method: CTC (crush-tear-curl)the leaf is cut into small granules; a strong, fast-brewing tea
Type: black, green, white, oolongset by the degree of oxidation (the broken leaf reacting with air, which darkens it): black is fully oxidised, green is not oxidised, oolong is partly oxidised, white is minimally processed (withered and dried, so only lightly oxidised)

Bengal's tea, region by region:

WhatDetail
RankIndia's 2nd-largest tea producer, after Assam
Shareabout 30%: 421.63 of India's 1,395.53 million kg in 2025 (30.2%); 30.7% in 2025-26
Darjeeling hillsorthodox, mainly black tea, plus some green, white and oolong; 87 GI gardens, about 17,500 ha
Dooars (Jalpaiguri, Alipurduar) and Terai (Siliguri plains)about 99% of WB tea (2025), mostly CTC black tea; no GI, only a Tea Board "Dooars Terai" logo
First GIDarjeeling Tea was India's first GI-tagged product (2004)
AuctionsKolkata: first auction 1861; sells CTC, orthodox and Darjeeling. Siliguri: opened 1976; CTC only
Tea Board of Indiaset up on 1 April 1954 under the Tea Act, 1953; headquarters in Kolkata
Tea Board offices in WBSiliguri zonal office and quality-control lab; Darjeeling Tea Research & Development Centre and a sub-regional office at Kurseong; regional offices at Jalpaiguri and Islampur (Uttar Dinajpur)

A GI tag (Geographical Indication) is a legal label saying a product comes from a particular place and owes its quality to it.

Examiner's twist

Do not set "orthodox" against "black tea". Orthodox and CTC are methods; black, green, white and oolong are types. Darjeeling's orthodox tea is mostly black, and Dooars–Terai CTC tea is black too. The pair to remember: hills = orthodox, plains = CTC.

Remember for the exam

WB is 2nd after Assam (about 30%). Darjeeling = orthodox (87 GI gardens); Dooars/Terai = CTC, about 99% of WB tea. Tea Board: Tea Act 1953, set up 1 April 1954, HQ Kolkata.

The Dooars and Terai tea gardens mostly produce:

  1. CTC tea
  2. Orthodox tea
  3. White tea
Tea: hills vs plains
Darjeeling hillsDooars and Terai plains
Orthodox teaCTC (crush-tear-curl)
~87 gardens, GI 2004Jalpaiguri, Alipurduar, Siliguri

In Shantipur you can still hear the clack of handlooms from village homes. Bengal's sarees and silk are known all over India.

WhatDetail
Maldaleading mulberry-silk district; Malda Nistari Silk Yarn GI (2025)
Murshidabadfamous for its silk (Murshidabad Silk GI, 2025-26)
BaluchariBishnupur, Bankura; silk with scenes from the epics woven in
Shantipur and Dhaniakhalicotton sarees
Tangailcotton; Phulia (Nadia) and Purba Bardhaman; GI 2024 as "Tangail Saree of Bengal"
Garadmulberry silk, white body with a coloured (traditionally red) border; Murshidabad and Birbhum; GI 2024
Korialheavier mulberry-silk bridal saree with a red border and rich zari; Murshidabad and Birbhum; GI 2024
State supportWB Textile Incentive Scheme 2022
Power loomsaround 1,400 power-loom units set up in the three years up to 2024
Examiner's twist

Baluchari sarees come from Bishnupur (Bankura), not Murshidabad, even though both are silk.

Remember for the exam

Baluchari = Bishnupur. Shantipur, Dhaniakhali and Tangail = cotton. Garad and Korial = silk (Murshidabad, Birbhum). Tangail, Garad, Korial: GI 2024. Malda = mulberry silk.

Baluchari sarees are traditionally woven at:

  1. Bishnupur
  2. Shantipur
  3. Krishnanagar

At a Kolkata handicraft fair you will see the Bankura horse, dokra figures and Chhau masks side by side. Many of these carry GI tags. West Bengal has 59 registered GIs: 58 West Bengal-only, plus Dalle Khursani (a chilli), which is shared with Sikkim. Since the batch certified on 27 March 2026, WB is 3rd in India, after Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu (count as of 31 March 2026).

Madur kathimats, Medinipur

Textile GIs (12): Santipore Saree (the Shantipur saree), Baluchari, Dhaniakhali, Tangail Saree of Bengal, Garad, Korial, Banglar Muslin, Begampur Cotton Handloom Saree, Murshidabad Silk, Malda Nistari Silk Yarn, Santiniketan Batik and Nakshi Kantha. Why it matters for an IDO: GI products are ready-made MSME clusters (groups of small units making the same product in one place). Branding, common facility centres and export links for them are typical IDO projects.

Examiner's twist

Dokra is metal casting, while terracotta is baked clay. Both are linked to Bankura.

Remember for the exam

WB has 59 GIs (58 WB-only + Dalle Khursani, shared with Sikkim), 3rd after UP and Tamil Nadu. Dokra = lost-wax metal casting.

Dokra craft of Bengal is a form of:

  1. Lost-wax metal casting
  2. Clay modelling
  3. Wood carving

sections.h: GI-tagged food, and the two years to know
sections.html:
Bengal's sweets, rice and mangoes are GI-tagged too.

Number trick

GI years: Darjeeling Tea 2004 (India's first) and Banglar Rasogolla 2017. Tea came 13 years before the sweet.

Remember for the exam

• Jute mills: 89 of India's 120 in WB (Dec 2025); WB grows about three-quarters of India's raw jute.

  • JPM Act, 1987: foodgrains and sugar must go in jute bags.
  • Tea: WB 2nd after Assam (about 30%). Darjeeling = orthodox, mainly black (87 GI gardens); Dooars/Terai = CTC black, about 99% of WB tea, no GI.
  • Tea Board (Tea Act 1953, from 1 April 1954), National Jute Board and JCI: HQ Kolkata. Tea auctions: Kolkata 1861; Siliguri 1976, CTC only.
  • Baluchari = Bishnupur (Bankura); Garad and Korial (silk) and Tangail (cotton): GI 2024; Malda and Murshidabad = silk.
  • 59 GIs (58 WB-only + Dalle Khursani), 3rd after UP and Tamil Nadu since 27 March 2026; 24 added in 2025-26.
  • Darjeeling Tea first GI (2004); Rasogolla 2017.
Examiner's twist

The Tea Board is headquartered in Kolkata. Its Siliguri office is a zonal (Aanchalik) one.

mcqs.q: As of December 2025, how many of India's 120 composite jute mills were located in West Bengal?
mcqs.e: West Bengal had 89 of the 120 mills, the highest of any state.

mcqs.q: The first product in India to receive a GI tag was:
mcqs.e: Darjeeling Tea was registered as India's first GI in 2004. Banglar Rasogolla got its tag in 2017.

mcqs.q: The Dooars and Terai tea gardens mostly produce:
mcqs.e: The Dooars and Terai mainly produce CTC black tea, while the Darjeeling hills produce orthodox tea, mainly black.

mcqs.q: Baluchari sarees are traditionally woven at:
mcqs.e: Baluchari silk sarees are a Bishnupur (Bankura) speciality. Shantipur and Dhaniakhali are known for cotton sarees, and Krishnanagar for clay dolls.

mcqs.q: Which Act mandates the use of jute bags for packing foodgrains?
mcqs.e: The Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory Use in Packing Commodities) Act, 1987 gives the mills a guaranteed source of demand.

mcqs.q: 'Tossa' jute is the common name of:
mcqs.e: Tossa is Corchorus olitorius and white jute is C. capsularis. Hibiscus cannabinus is mesta, and Crotalaria juncea is sunn hemp.

mcqs.q: Dokra craft of Bengal is a form of:
mcqs.e: Dokra is non-ferrous metal casting (metals other than iron) by the lost-wax method, practised in Bankura and Bardhaman.

mcqs.q: The headquarters of the Tea Board of India is at:
mcqs.e: The Tea Board is headquartered in Kolkata. Its Siliguri office is a zonal (Aanchalik) one.

mcqs.q: Fazli, Laxmanbhog and Himsagar are GI-tagged varieties of mango associated with:
mcqs.e: Malda is the mango belt of the state.

mcqs.q: India's approximate share of world jute-goods production is:
mcqs.e: India produces about 75% of the world's jute goods.

mcqs.q: The Tea Board of India was set up under:
mcqs.e: The Tea Board was set up on 1 April 1954 under the Tea Act, 1953. Its headquarters is in Kolkata.

mcqs.q: The Siliguri tea auction centre, opened in 1976, sells:
mcqs.e: Siliguri sells only CTC tea from the North Bengal plains. Darjeeling and orthodox teas are sold at Kolkata, India's first tea auction (1861).

mcqs.q: After the GI batch of 27 March 2026, West Bengal's GI count and national rank were:
o: 59; 3rd after Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
mcqs.e: WB has 59 GIs (58 WB-only plus Dalle Khursani, shared with Sikkim) and is 3rd. The 24 is the number added in 2025-26, when WB was 2nd that year after Madhya Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Garad sarees of Murshidabad and Birbhum are woven from:
mcqs.e: Garad is a mulberry-silk saree with a white body and a coloured (traditionally red) border; it got its GI in 2024.
